text:
Full-Time School with ME/CFS This week I went back to school for a full-time online course. My initial infection was in February 2024. In 2025, I was able to return to part-time work, although not on a regular basis. My main symptoms are PEM and vertigo, and I would consider my Long COVID/ME/CFS to be mild.

The course runs until September, and I'm honestly not sure whether I can sustain it for that long. It's only Saturday, and I'm already feeling extremely exhausted.

I also started taking fluvoxamine this week, and my sleep has been worse since then. My current medications are LDN, LDA, amifampridine, and fluvoxamine. In addition, I regularly use a red light mat, nicotine patches, and do HBOT twice a week. This week I was only able to do HBOT once, so maybe that's contributing to the increased fatigue.

I'm struggling to decide whether I should continue with school. For those of you with Long COVID or ME/CFS who have returned to full-time work or school, how long did it take for your body to adjust, if it did at all?

To be honest, I spent most of today crying. I was doing relatively well until Thursday, but then the PEM started to hit, and the exhaustion has been overwhelming.
notes: REAL post t3_1tyd1cr. OBSERVED FAILURE #2 (side-effect over-attribution). Author attributes worse sleep ONLY to fluvoxamine ('I also started taking fluvoxamine this week, and my sleep has been worse since then'). This is NOT a LIST FANOUT (the symptom is tied to one drug the author started, not predicated of a drug list), so 'worse sleep' must attach to fluvoxamine alone. The prior pipeline run wrongly put 'worse sleep' on red light mat + nicotine patches + hbot (see data/posts.db) -- this row pins that bug: those three are a stable pre-existing stack with no symptom attributed and no benefit claimed => neutral, side_effects=[]. fluvoxamine => negative + side_effects=['worse sleep']. LDN/LDA/amifampridine left UNLABELED: named in the stack with no individual outcome and the week went badly (PEM/crying), so sentiment is genuinely ambiguous. expected_drugs: extract must find all 7; LDA (low-dose abilify) must not be confused with / dropped for LDN.

text: Yes, I attribute this to the neuro/energy issues. Once I started to have more energy due to ldn, it was like all of the delayed emotional and psychological processing started. "I think I only now have enough energy to reflect on everything that's happened...it's like I had to put it all on pause. I have a lot of feelings to work through still. I'm playing catch up, it comes in waves."

text: It won't do much without the appropriate diet. But in general the mast cells need quite some time to stabilise again. Ketotifen it's the first line treatment here with antihistamines and needs weeks to be effective. Antihistamines only block some receptors, for only sums hours, histamine can still cause a lot of symptoms, mast cells are still releasing histamine. Ketotifen actually stabilises the mast cells and treats the actual cause. Desloratadine can also be mast cell stabilising. Also it depends on which ones you're taking Zyrtec would make you tired on it's own, ehybitd barely used here
